Q1: A great city fire. A caption reads 'The Great Fire' (1666). Flames spread through the dense wooden, half-timbered houses over several days, from 2 to 5 Sept 1666.
Q2: One small place. It starts in a single bakery with an oven fire (a baker is named on screen). It then shows a narrow street with a few houses burning, and only afterwards the fire spreading across the wider district. A map near the river marks the small start area (a lane near the bridge).
Q3: They flee on foot and in carts piled with bundles and furniture. They load belongings into rowing boats and escape across the Thames. Crowds also cross the bridge. Survivors end up camping in open fields in tents beside small fires. The pictures show no organised firefighting in 1666.
Q4: Not sure. Around frames 49–50 (196–200s) a large church-like building with a tower stands in the glowing, burning city. The pictures do not clearly show it burning or collapsing. Later a ruined church tower stands among the rubble (frame 69).
Q5: In brick, with scaffolding and brick-laying shown, and some stone. It is rebuilt largely on the old street layout. A surveyor with stakes marks out plots, and a court-like hearing is held, apparently about plots or boundaries. A plan with a new regular grid is shown, but the finished city has an irregular layout like the old one.
Q6: A large white domed cathedral rises over the red-brick roofs, with its dome completed around 1710–11. A caption reads 'The dome rules the skyline'. A tall stone column (the Monument, labelled 202 ft) stands near the river and is shown with an engraving.
Q7: Bombing sets the city on fire again. Dated 29–30 Dec 1940 and captioned 'The second great fire', the night sky glows with fire, firefighters work at the river and on rooftops, and a count of incendiaries appears. The big domed cathedral still stands lit amid the flames. A large area is burnt and marked in orange.
Q8: A modern city, 2026, of glass and concrete towers and office blocks beside the river with bridges. By night the windows are lit. The old domed cathedral is still visible among the towers.

lost.why: Several nearly black frames (10–12, 59–63) with no clear content.
Opening jumps between 2026, 1881 and 1738 with no clear link.
Sudden jump to 1647 with an engraving inset, then back to 2 Sept 1666.
Church on the hill is hard to make out in the glowing fire, and its fate is not clearly shown.
Indoor hearing scene: unclear what is being decided.
Jump to 1938 and then 1666 before 1940, with no clear reason.
Flashes back to 2 Sept 1666 after the modern city.
